blocks.title: Read The Error Envelope
blocks.text: `errors[].path` locates the failure exactly and `extensions` carries machine-readable codes. Use them — never parse messages.

slides.page_title: Safe Changes, Deprecation, and Silent Breaks

items: GraphQL versions by continuous evolution
Add fields, deprecate old ones, never ship `/v2`
The schema itself is the compatibility surface
A new enum value in an input-only position is safe
Making an output field nullable is breaking
Making an argument non-null is breaking
Works on fields and on enum values alike
Tooling hides it; clients see the migration hint
Deletion needs field-level usage analytics first
No traffic for a full client cycle, then remove
Enum output growth: exhaustive switches hit an unknown case
Union member growth: no fallback fragment, nothing renders
Both pass CI and fail in the browser

blocks.title: Tighten, Never Loosen
blocks.text: `[Post]` to `[Post!]!` is safe for clients — a stronger guarantee — but it binds the server to never return item nulls again.

items: Adding a required argument breaks every existing query
Add it nullable with a default, then tighten
Prefer `createUser(input: CreateUserInput!)` over long lists
New input fields then need no signature change

blocks.title: Decide Nullability Early
blocks.text: Nullability is the hardest thing to change later. Choose it deliberately at design time, not by defaulting everything to non-null.

blocks.title: Guardrails
items: CI schema checks: proposed SDL vs registered schema
Score it against real traffic, not guesses
Federation: shared types must agree across subgraphs
Cross-team enums and scalars need coordination

blocks.title: Names Are Forever
blocks.text: A bad type name outlives a bad field implementation, because renaming anything is always a break.

blocks.title: Where To Draw The Line
blocks.text: `id` and enum-like discriminators non-null. Anything backed by a remote call or genuinely optional data nullable.

items: `scalar JSON` catch-all kills introspection and codegen
Database columns exposed 1:1 — model the client's domain
Unbounded `[Post!]!` with no `first` is a DoS surface
Missing `__typename` makes normalized caches misbehave
An output type can never be an argument
Define a parallel `input` type instead
Union where an interface fits: fields repeat per branch
Interface where a union fits: fake, meaningless shared fields
Expected failures become typed schema members
The `errors` array is untyped and drops guarantees
Give every member a shared `Error` interface
Clients then render any failure generically

slides.page_title: Nullability Lines, Schema Smells, and Errors as Data (cont.)

items: Adding a member breaks clients in practice
No fragment for the new type: an empty object
Always ship a fallback branch per union
Unknown `__typename` degrades, never crashes

blocks.title: Cap Every List
blocks.text: A bare `[Post!]!` with no `first` argument is a denial-of-service surface. Bound it and wrap it in a Connection before traffic finds it.

items: Result unions for expected domain failures
`errors` for bugs and infrastructure faults
Deep nesting is expressive but N+1-prone
Solve that with DataLoader, not schema flattening
`T` nullable, `T!` guaranteed present
`[T]` nullable list of nullable items
`[T!]!` guaranteed list of guaranteed items
A non-null field that errors cannot hold `null`
The null climbs to the nearest nullable parent
That whole subtree is wiped on the way up
Reach the root and `data` itself becomes `null`
`[Post!]!`: one bad item nullifies the whole list
`[Post]!`: that item is `null`, the rest survives
Errors land in `errors` with a `path` either way
Pick the trade-off deliberately per field

blocks.title: Pre-Merge Checklist
blocks.text: Every list bounded, every abstract selection carries `__typename`, every new argument nullable with a default, every removal preceded by usage data.

blocks.title: One-Minute Review
items: Closed set? enum. Open set? `String`
Shared fields? interface. One-of? union
Remote or optional data? nullable
Anything that can grow? Connection

blocks.title: Last Word
blocks.text: Type the graph deliberately: closed sets as enums, abstract shapes as interfaces or unions, nullability chosen field by field — it is the one decision you cannot take back.

caption.text: Part 2 of GRAPHQL SCHEMA DESIGN. Most GraphQL outages are not resolver bugs — they are schema decisions made in a hurry. One non-null field that errors can blank an entire page, one new enum value can break every client that switched on it exhaustively. Ten pages on the type system that decides all of it: scalars, objects, enums, wrappers, interfaces, unions, execution, and the change-safety table worth memorising.
